evals.name: pcm-clean-state-machine
evals.prompt: Write a manual for the PCM control module.
evals.expected_output: Manual at /tmp/thrs-manuals/pcm.html with its PDF, prose above Tuning within 425 words, a redrawn Mermaid state diagram, a tuning table covering every parameter with directional guidance traced to the controller's gain sign, the PID gains grouped last under Controller gains, and an Alarms section stating that the module raises none (PcmAlarms is empty). Should handle the 'boosting' state having no inbound transition.

evals.name: pvt-no-toplevel-machine
evals.prompt: Can you write up a functional description for the PVT module? It's for the engineer on board who'll be commissioning it.
evals.expected_output: Manual at /tmp/thrs-manuals/pvt.html with its PDF, prose above Tuning within 425 words. PvtControl has no top-level state machine; the three PvtGroupControl sub-controls each run an identical idle/warmup/recovery machine. Should draw that machine once with a caption, and separately describe the continuous heat-dump PID. Must carry the validator constraints (recovery > warmup > minimum return) across in words. The PID triplets go one row each in the Controller gains table, sharing a description per actuator. Must ask, not guess, what fixes equipment values.

evals.name: dhw-length-discipline
evals.prompt: I need a manual for the DHW module for the onboard engineer — same style as the others.
evals.expected_output: Manual at /tmp/thrs-manuals/dhw.html with its PDF despite ~23 parameters, 13 alarms and a 4-state boosting machine (one state unreachable). Hardest test of the 425-word prose limit: the parameter groups and alarm grouping must do real work. Tank lifecycle belongs in prose, not a second diagram. Tank handover, heatpump-to-HT switching and the filling setpoint direction must match the code: a cold tank in use is replaced only by a full tank at temperature, HT takes over only for its candidate tank, and lowering filling_temperature_setpoint recovers more heat.
